name: Rice Kheer

ingredients.name: Basmati rice, broken or short-grain if possible (chawal)

equipment: Small heavy-bottomed saucepan or deep non-stick pan: a heavy base spreads the heat and lowers the risk of scorching
Wooden spoon or ladle with a flat back: for stirring and pressing the rice
Small bowl and a fine sieve: for rinsing and soaking the rice
Measuring spoons, measuring jug or cup, kitchen scale (or use the household measures), small knife and board for the nuts
Pressure cooker (optional): not needed here; the source recipes that use it differ in timing, so this recipe does not

steps.title: Measure the rice
steps.text: Measure 10 g (2 tsp) basmati rice into a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small level heap of white grains covering the bottom of the bowl
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the bowl, next to a 1 tsp spoon
steps.videoShot: A spoon levelling 2 tsp of rice into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Too much rice, which turns the kheer into a thick, porridge-like pudding; stick to 2 tsp for 200 ml milk.

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Cover the rice with water, swirl, pour the cloudy water off and repeat 2-3 times.
steps.visualCue: The water goes from milky to almost clear
steps.cameraCheck: The final rinse water, nearly clear
steps.videoShot: Water swirling milky white and then running clear.
steps.watchOut: Pouring grains out with the water; tip slowly and hold the sieve or your hand against the bowl's edge, and if some grains escape, tip them back in.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Leave the rinsed rice in 60 ml of fresh water for 20 min.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn chalky white and look slightly swollen, and one grain snaps easily between two fingers
steps.cameraCheck: The soaking bowl with the timer visible
steps.videoShot: Rice sitting in water, and a timer set to 20 min.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the soak, which makes the rice take much longer to soften in the milk; if you are short of time, give it 10 min and add 5 min to step 8.

steps.title: Prepare the nuts and cardamom
steps.text: Slice 3 almonds and 4 pistachios thinly. Open 2 cardamom pods and crush the seeds with the back of a spoon in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Thin nut slivers, and a coarse brown-black cardamom powder that smells sweet and floral
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced nuts and crushed cardamom in two small bowls
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing an almond into thin slivers.
steps.watchOut: Thick chunks of nut, which stay hard; slice thin or lightly crush them. A weak smell means the cardamom is old; use 3 pods instead.

steps.title: Rinse the pan
steps.text: Swirl 2 tbsp water around the saucepan and tip it out, leaving the pan wet.
steps.visualCue: A thin film of water over the whole base of the pan
steps.videoShot: Water swirling inside the pan and being poured out.
steps.watchOut: A dry pan, where the first milk can stick and brown; the wet film helps stop that (Tarla Dalal's tip). Do not leave pools of water, as they dilute the milk.

steps.title: Heat the milk
steps.text: Pour 200 ml milk into the pan, set it on medium heat and stir every 30 seconds until bubbles form around the edge and the milk is about to boil.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles ring the edge and steam rises; a thin skin begins to form
steps.cameraCheck: The pan of milk with bubbles at the edge
steps.videoShot: Bubbles forming round the edge of the milk.
steps.watchOut: Milk boiling over when left alone; stay at the stove, and if it rises quickly, lift the pan off the heat for a few seconds and stir.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and add it to the hot milk, then turn the heat to low. If using saffron, drop in 3 threads now.
steps.visualCue: The rice sinks, then the milk calms to a gentle bubble only at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the pan with the flame on low
steps.videoShot: Drained rice sliding into the milk.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the heat on medium, which scorches the bottom and gives a brown, burnt smell; keep it on low from here, and if you smell burning, do not scrape the bottom, move the kheer to a clean pan.

steps.title: Simmer and stir
steps.text: Simmer on low for about 25 min, stirring every 2-3 min and scraping the bottom and sides.
steps.tip: Set a timer for every 3 min as a reminder to stir.
steps.visualCue: The milk slowly thickens and turns slightly creamy-beige, the volume drops by about a third, and the rice grains are soft and swollen
steps.cameraCheck: The pan at the 15 min mark, to show the milk thickening
steps.videoShot: A spoon scraping the base of the pan.
steps.watchOut: A skin of milk solids on top and a layer sticking to the base; stir the skin back in, and if the base starts to stick, lower the heat. The sources give 30-75 min for 1 litre, so a small batch can finish earlier or later: keep going until the grains are soft.

steps.title: Mash a few grains
steps.text: Press a few rice grains against the side of the pan with the back of the spoon for about 1 min.
steps.visualCue: Soft grains squash easily and the milk turns slightly cloudy and creamier
steps.cameraCheck: The back of the spoon pressing grains against the pan
steps.videoShot: Grains being squashed against the side of the pan.
steps.watchOut: Mashing all the rice into a paste (it becomes gluey); crush only about a third of the grains. Broken or short-grain rice needs no mashing.

steps.title: Add the sugar
steps.text: Add 20 g (4 tsp) sugar and stir for 2 min until it is dissolved.
steps.visualCue: No visible crystals at the bottom, and the kheer looks a little thinner right after the sugar goes in
steps.cameraCheck: The spoon lifted out clean, with no crystals
steps.videoShot: Sugar sprinkled in and stirred until it vanishes.
steps.watchOut: Adding the sugar too early, which can keep the rice firm, and over-sweetening. Add it once the rice is soft, then taste and add up to 1 tsp more if wanted.

steps.title: Add cardamom and raisins
steps.text: Stir in the crushed cardamom and 5 g (8-10) raisins.
steps.visualCue: A sweet, floral smell rises and the raisins start to plump
steps.cameraCheck: The kheer with cardamom and raisins stirred in
steps.videoShot: Cardamom powder falling into the pan.
steps.watchOut: Cardamom husks in the pan, which are hard to chew; keep only the crushed seeds.

steps.title: Simmer to thicken
steps.text: Simmer 3-5 min more on low, stirring.
steps.visualCue: The kheer coats the back of the spoon, and a line drawn through it with a finger stays for a second or two
steps.cameraCheck: A spoon coated with kheer, with the finger line
steps.videoShot: Kheer dripping slowly off the spoon.
steps.watchOut: Over-thickening, since kheer firms up a lot as it cools; stop while it is still a little looser than you want it, and if it gets too thick, stir in 2 tbsp warm milk or water.

steps.title: Finish with nuts
steps.text: Turn off the heat, then stir in half the sliced almonds and pistachios. Keep the rest for the top.
steps.visualCue: Cream-coloured kheer with green and pale nut slivers through it
steps.cameraCheck: The finished kheer in the pan
steps.videoShot: Nuts being stirred in at the end.
steps.watchOut: Adding the nuts too early, so they go soft; keep them to the end for a little bite.

steps.title: Cool and serve
steps.text: Pour into a bowl, scatter the remaining nuts on top and let it cool for 10 min. Serve warm or chill it.
steps.visualCue: A creamy, slightly thick pudding that settles and thickens as it cools
steps.cameraCheck: The finished bowl of kheer with nuts on top
steps.videoShot: A spoon lifting a creamy spoonful from the bowl.
steps.watchOut: A film forming on top while it cools; cover with a plate or stir it in. If it is too thick when cold, loosen it with a splash of cold milk.

reasons: a dessert with little oil, no frying, no salt and a useful amount of calcium (about 25% of the day), riboflavin and B12 from the milk, with moderate saturated fat (about 4.6 g). Points off for about 20 g of added sugar (80% of the 25 g limit), almost no fibre (about 1 g) and refined white rice. Restaurant versions often use more sugar, khoya or cream, and larger bowls, so a higher-calorie, sweeter portion is likely (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published, much-loved festival and home dessert, with many recipe sites, blogs and cooking channels describing the same basic rice-milk-sugar-cardamom recipe. Points off because it takes patient stirring and a long simmer, and results vary with the rice and milk fat. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed container for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour of cooking). Freezing is not recommended (the milk can separate and the rice turns grainy on thawing; not source-checked). It sets thick in the fridge; reheat in a pan on low heat with 2-3 tbsp milk, stirring until smooth and warm, or microwave in 30 second bursts, stirring in between.
leftoverRemix: Kheer pancakes (kheer malpua-style). Mix 3 tbsp leftover kheer with 2 tbsp whole-wheat flour and a pinch of fennel seeds to a thick batter, and shallow-fry small spoonfuls in a little ghee until golden on both sides (contains gluten).
burnOff: about 4.1 km of running (290 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 10 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: rice is a grain and is not eaten in most vrat rule sets; swap the rice for sama ke chawal (barnyard millet) or makhana and use sugar or rock sugar (assumption: the common rule set; families differ; the swap is common vrat practice but was not source-checked this run)

ekadashi.reason: grains are avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set, so swap the rice for sama (barnyard millet) or sabudana (not source-checked this run; families differ)

jain.reason: no roots, onion, garlic, meat, fish, egg or honey in the recipe

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a sweet, milky bowl that is gentle at iftar or sehri, but high in sugar (about 20 g added), so keep to one small bowl

jain.reason: milk, rice, sugar, cardamom, raisins and nuts only; no onion, garlic, potato or other root vegetable, no egg, no honey (some Jain families avoid certain sugars or dried fruit on specific days; families differ)

vegan.reason: the main recipe uses cow milk (200 ml); use thick coconut milk (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: the recipe has no onion or garlic

glutenFree.reason: rice, milk, sugar, cardamom and nuts; no wheat, rava, maida or hing

dairyFree.reason: milk; use the coconut-milk version (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: Main recipe already Jain (no onion, garlic, roots, egg or honey).
Main recipe already gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing).
